Healthy.explanation: The tomato plant shows optimal physiological vigor, vibrant green foliage, strong stems, and zero signs of foliar blight, bacterial specking, or viral distortion.
symptoms: Uniform deep green leaf lamina with intact serrated margins
Firm erect stems and healthy cluster flowering
Absence of chlorotic halos, necrotic spots, or leaf curling
culturalActions: Maintain consistent drip or furrow irrigation to prevent moisture stress and blossom-end rot
Prune lower suckers near soil level to optimize airflow and minimize soil-splash contamination
Provide sturdy stakes or trellising to keep foliage and fruit elevated above wet soil
prevention: Rotate tomato planting with non-solanaceous crops (e.g. maize, legumes) every 2-3 seasons
Use certified pathogen-free hybrid seeds with high germination vigor
Apply organic straw mulch around plant bases to conserve moisture and suppress weeds
Healthy.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR) & TNAU Agritech
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Early Blight.explanation: Early Blight (Alternaria solani) is a prevalent fungal foliar disease producing distinctive concentric target-board brown lesions, beginning on older lower foliage.
symptoms: Circular dark brown to black spots with characteristic concentric rings (target pattern)
Chlorotic yellowing surrounding necrotic spots, progressing to premature defoliation
Stem collar lesions and dark sunken leathery spots at stem ends of fruits
culturalActions: Promptly rogue and destroy severely spotted lower leaves to reduce airborne inoculum
Switch from sprinkler/overhead watering to ground-level drip irrigation to keep canopy dry
Space plants adequately (60 cm × 45 cm) to facilitate thorough air circulation
prevention: Treat seeds prior to sowing using certified biocontrol agents (Trichoderma viride at 4g/kg seed)
Deep plow crop residues immediately post-harvest to accelerate fungal decomposition
Follow a strict 3-year crop rotation avoiding potato, eggplant, and chili
Early Blight.source: ICAR - Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) & DPPQS
Early Blight.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Late Blight.explanation: Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) is an aggressive water mold pathogen thriving under cool, humid conditions, causing rapid foliar decay and fruit rot.
symptoms: Irregular water-soaked dark lesions appearing rapidly on leaf tips and margins
White delicate downy fungal growth visible on leaf undersides during humid mornings
Dark greasy firm rot patches spreading across green and ripe tomato fruits
culturalActions: Immediately remove and deeply bury blighted plant sections to contain rapid field spread
Avoid working in tomato fields when leaves are wet to prevent spreading spores
Ensure field ditches and furrows provide rapid drainage after heavy rainfall
prevention: Plant certified resistant varieties recommended by state agricultural universities
Enforce wide row spacing and north-south ridge orientation for rapid sun-drying of foliage
Apply preventive bio-formulations during prolonged foggy or high-humidity spells
Late Blight.source: ICAR - Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI) & IIVR
Late Blight.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Bacterial Spot.explanation: Bacterial Spot (Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria) causes small water-soaked dark flecks that turn necrotic and scab-like on both leaves and fruit.
symptoms: Small, circular to angular water-soaked dark spots on leaves with yellow halos
Severely infected leaves turn yellow, blister, and drop prematurely
Slightly raised brown scab-like spots with rough margins on tomato fruit
culturalActions: Eliminate weed hosts and wild nightshade species around greenhouse and field borders
Sterilize farm pruning shears and harvest crates with certified disinfectant solution
Avoid sprinkler or rain-gun irrigation that splashes bacterial slime between plants
prevention: Source disease-free seed tested for bacterial contamination
Soak nursery seeds in hot water (50°C for 25 minutes) before planting
Practice strict rotation with corn, sorghum, or legumes
Bacterial Spot.source: ICAR - Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) Plant Pathology
Bacterial Spot.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.explanation: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV) is a debilitating begomovirus transmitted by silverleaf whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci), inducing severe stunting and leaf deformation.
symptoms: Marked upward curling and cupping of leaflets with chlorotic yellow margins
Interveinal chlorosis, reduction in leaf lamina size, and crinkled texture
Severe plant stunting with flower drop, leading to virtually zero fruit set
culturalActions: Install yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre) uniformly across the field to monitor whitefly vectors
Erect 40-50 mesh insect-proof nylon netting around nursery seedbeds
Promptly uproot and burn virus-infected stunt plants to prevent vector transmission
prevention: Sow TYLCV-tolerant hybrid cultivars recommended for your agro-climatic zone
Plant border barrier crops of maize or pearl millet (3 rows) around the tomato plot
Spray botanical neem formulation (Azadirachtin 1500 ppm at 3ml/L) to deter whitefly colonization
Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.source: ICAR - National Research Centre for Integrated Pest Management (NCIPM)
Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: The maize crop exhibits healthy broad leaf blades, deep green chlorophyll pigmentation, robust central midribs, intact protective husks, and uniform golden kernels.
symptoms: Uniform green corn leaf lamina with smooth margins and erect posture
Clean central midrib without reddish streak lesions, chlorosis, or necrotic spots
Well-filled uniform ear with healthy golden yellow kernels and fresh silks
culturalActions: Ensure consistent irrigation during critical tasseling and silking growth stages
Split nitrogen applications (basal, knee-high, and pre-tasseling) to maximize nutrient uptake
Conduct regular field scouting to monitor ear health and beneficial insect populations
prevention: Sow certified hybrid maize seed with verified high germination vigor
Implement field crop rotation with leguminous pulses (gram, soybean, or moong)
Store harvested grain at safe moisture levels (below 12-14%) in sanitized, pest-proof bins
Healthy.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR)
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Common Rust.explanation: Common Rust (Puccinia sorghi) is a foliar fungal pathogen producing cinnamon-brown powdery pustules across both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
symptoms: Small, circular to elongated cinnamon-brown pustules (uredinia) scattered on leaves
Powdery brick-red spores released upon rupture of the leaf epidermis
Pustules turning brownish-black late in the season as resting spores (teliospores) form
culturalActions: Avoid excess nitrogen fertilization that promotes overly lush, susceptible foliage
Maintain recommended plant population density (60,000-65,000 plants/ha) to facilitate airflow
Irrigate in early morning so canopy surfaces dry quickly under sunlight
prevention: Plant rust-resistant certified hybrid maize cultivars adapted to local climate
Sow at the earliest recommended agronomic window to avoid peak late-season rust spore showers
Destroy volunteer maize stalks and perennial host grasses near field borders
Common Rust.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) & PAU
Common Rust.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Gray Leaf Spot.explanation: Gray Leaf Spot (Cercospora zeae-maydis) is a damaging fungal foliar disease causing distinct rectangular tan-to-gray lesions bounded strictly by leaf veins.
symptoms: Rectangular elongated lesions parallel to leaf veins with sharp distinct borders
Lesions turn grayish-tan under humid conditions due to fungal sporulation
Coalescence of lesions resulting in extensive foliar blighting and premature stalk dry-down
culturalActions: Incorporate infected crop residue through deep summer plowing to accelerate residue breakdown
Rotate fields out of maize for at least one full crop season using soybean or cotton
Scout lower leaves starting at 8-leaf vegetative stage through silking
prevention: Select certified hybrid varieties with moderate to high genetic resistance ratings
Avoid continuous monocropping of maize on fields with history of gray leaf spot
Ensure balanced balanced potassium fertilization to bolster leaf structural cell walls
Gray Leaf Spot.source: ICAR - Directorate of Maize Research (DMR) / IIMR
Gray Leaf Spot.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Northern Leaf Blight.explanation: Northern Corn Leaf Blight (Exserohilum turcicum) is a major fungal disease producing large cigar-shaped elliptical grayish-green necrotic lesions.
symptoms: Large elliptical cigar-shaped lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long) on foliage
Lesions start grayish-green, turning tan or grayish-brown as tissue dies
Dark sooty sporulation rings visible inside lesions during humid morning hours
culturalActions: Chop and deeply plow maize stubble post-harvest to reduce overwintering conidia
Optimize row spacing to prevent prolonged microclimate humidity within canopy
Rogue severely blighted seedlings in early growth stages
prevention: Sow certified disease-tolerant maize hybrids with multi-genic resistance
Practice 2-year crop rotation with non-graminaceous crops
Ensure timely sowing according to regional university agricultural calendars
Northern Leaf Blight.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) Plant Pathology
Northern Leaf Blight.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Maize Streak Virus.explanation: Maize Streak Virus (MSV) is a leafhopper-vectored (Cicadulina spp.) mastrevirus causing continuous chlorotic yellow-white streaks parallel to leaf veins.
symptoms: Tiny round chlorotic spots developing into continuous narrow streaks along veins
Streaks appear uniformly on all leaves emerging after the point of infection
Severe stunting, shortened internodes, and undersized or barren ears
culturalActions: Maintain strict weed-free buffer zones around fields to eliminate leafhopper refuges
Avoid staggered planting dates within the same locality to break vector breeding cycles
Rogue and bury severely stunted symptomatic plants during early vegetative stages
prevention: Sow MSV-resistant hybrid seed lots
Treat seeds prior to sowing with certified registered seed protectants
Coordinate synchronized community sowing dates across the village cluster
Maize Streak Virus.source: ICAR - National Research Centre for Integrated Pest Management (NCIPM)
Maize Streak Virus.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Fall Armyworm.explanation: Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) is an invasive noctuid pest whose larvae voraciously feed within the maize leaf whorl, shredding foliage and boring into developing ears.
symptoms: Pinholes and irregular window-pane feeding scratches on young whorl leaves
Severe ragged leaf tearing and abundant moist sawdust-like fecal frass in the whorl
Larva possesses inverted white 'Y' mark on head and 4 raised dark spots arranged in square on 8th abdominal segment
culturalActions: Conduct weekly whorl inspection starting 7 days after germination
Apply neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) or sand-lime mixture into whorls to suffocate young instars
Install pheromone traps (5 traps/acre) across field margins for early moth detection
prevention: Intercrop maize with pigeonpea, cowpea, or desmodium as push-pull pest deterrents
Conserve predatory earwigs, parasitoid wasps, and entomopathogenic fungi in field
Deep summer plow to expose pupae to predatory birds and intense solar radiation
Fall Armyworm.source: ICAR - National Bureau of Agricultural Insect Resources (NBAIR) & IIMR
Fall Armyworm.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: The paddy crop shows vibrant deep green upright tillers, clean leaf blades, healthy root aeration, and zero symptoms of blast, sheath rot, or bacterial blight.
symptoms: Uniform green erect leaf blades with smooth leaf margins
Clean leaf sheaths and collar regions without lesions or water-soaking
Healthy root system with reddish-brown oxidation halos indicating active oxygen transport
culturalActions: Follow Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) irrigation to conserve water and promote root vigor
Apply recommended dose of nitrogen split into 3-4 stages matching tiller formation and panicle initiation
Maintain clean bunds and weed-free field borders
prevention: Use certified paddy seed with germination vigor > 85%
Adopt System of Rice Intensification (SRI) spacing (25 cm × 25 cm) for robust tillering
Incorporate green manure (Dhaincha / Sunnhemp) before transplanting
Healthy.source: ICAR - National Rice Research Institute (NRRI), Cuttack
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Bacterial Leaf Blight.explanation: Bacterial Leaf Blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae) is a major bacterial disease causing water-soaked to yellowish-white undulating wavy stripes along leaf margins.
symptoms: Water-soaked lesions starting at leaf tips and wavy undulating margins
Lesions turn milky-white to straw-colored with translucent wavy margins
Bacterial ooze droplets visible on young lesions during early humid morning hours
culturalActions: Drain standing water from infected fields and suspend irrigation for 2-3 days
Withhold nitrogen top-dressing immediately; apply potassium to strengthen cell walls
Avoid handling or working in flooded fields while foliage is wet
prevention: Cultivate BLB-resistant varieties (e.g., Improved Samba Mahsuri, Swarna-Sub1 where recommended)
Soak seeds in hot water (52-54°C for 10 minutes) or certified bactericidal solution
Clip seedling leaf tips during transplanting only with sanitized implements
Bacterial Leaf Blight.source: ICAR - National Rice Research Institute (NRRI) & Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR)
Bacterial Leaf Blight.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Blast.explanation: Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae) is an airborne fungal disease producing characteristic spindle-shaped eye-like lesions on leaves, nodes, and neck joints of panicles.
symptoms: Spindle-shaped or elliptical lesions with grayish-white centers and dark brown margins
Lesions enlarge and coalesce, causing entire leaf blades to wither and dry
Neck blast causes blackening of panicle base, resulting in incomplete grain filling (chaffy grains)
culturalActions: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which creates soft, succulent vulnerable tissue
Keep field bunds clear of grassy weed alternate hosts like Echinochloa
Maintain continuous shallow flooding (2-5 cm) to suppress airborne spore inoculation
prevention: Sow certified blast-resistant cultivars adapted to your agro-climatic region
Treat seed with Trichoderma harzianum or certified seed dressing formulation
Avoid late transplanting during peak humid monsoon overcast periods
Blast.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad
Blast.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Brown Spot.explanation: Brown Spot (Bipolaris oryzae) is a fungal disease strongly associated with poor soil fertility, zinc deficiency, or drought stress, causing circular oval brown spots.
symptoms: Numerous small circular or oval sesame seed-like brown spots evenly across leaf blades
Mature spots feature a gray or light-brown center surrounded by a reddish-brown margin
Discoloration and black spotting of glumes and grain hulls
culturalActions: Correct underlying soil nutrient imbalances by applying balanced N-P-K along with Zinc Sulfate (25 kg/ha)
Maintain adequate irrigation; avoid moisture stress during vegetative growth
Apply decomposed farmyard manure (FYM at 10-12 t/ha) to improve soil organic carbon
prevention: Conduct seed treatment with hot water (54°C for 15 min) or certified biological inoculants
Test soil fertility before transplanting to ensure adequate potash and zinc availability
Burn or deeply incorporate stubble from severely spotted fields
Brown Spot.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Tungro.explanation: Rice Tungro Disease is caused by a joint viral infection (RTBV & RTSV) transmitted by green leafhoppers (Nephotettix virescens), causing intense stunting and orange-yellow discoloration.
symptoms: Leaves turn yellow to bright orange starting from leaf tips and margins
Young leaves mottled with pale green to white interveinal striping
Marked plant stunting, reduced tillering, and delayed panicle emergence
culturalActions: Monitor green leafhopper populations using light traps and sweep nets
Rogue and destroy infected hills early in nursery and tillering stages
Synchronize planting across the village to minimize vector migration windows
prevention: Sow tungro-resistant or GLH-resistant cultivars (e.g. Vikramarya, Radha)
Maintain clean bunds free of weed grass alternate hosts (Leersia hexandra)
Spray registered botanical neem formulation if vector density crosses economic threshold
Tungro.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR)
Tungro.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: The wheat crop displays vigorous upright tillering, clean lanceolate leaf blades, sturdy hollow culms, healthy emerging spikelets, and absence of rust or mildew pustules.
symptoms: Uniform glaucous green leaf blades with clean margins
Sturdy erect tillers with intact auricles and ligules
Uniform earhead emergence with well-developed spikelets
culturalActions: Provide critical crown root initiation (CRI) irrigation 20-25 days after sowing
Apply balanced nitrogen splitting (1/2 basal, 1/4 at CRI, 1/4 at late tillering)
Scout field twice weekly during flowering and grain-filling stages
prevention: Sow certified rust-resistant wheat varieties (e.g. HD-2967, HD-3086, DBW series)
Ensure timely sowing (first fortnight of November for North-Western Plains Zone)
Maintain optimal seed rate (100 kg/ha for timely sown irrigated conditions)
Healthy.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR), Karnal
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Brown Rust.explanation: Brown / Leaf Rust (Puccinia triticina) produces small round to oval orange-brown powdery pustules scattered randomly across the upper leaf surface.
symptoms: Small circular to oval orange-brown pustules distributed randomly on leaf blades
Orange powder rubs off on fingers; pustules rarely coalesce into linear stripes
Severely infected leaves turn yellow, senesce prematurely, and reduce grain weight
culturalActions: Avoid late sowing which exposes crop to high spring temperatures favored by brown rust
Maintain balanced potash fertilization to increase leaf epidermal resistance
Irrigate judiciously during boot and flowering stages
prevention: Cultivate certified multi-gene rust-resistant varieties recommended by IIWBR
Eradicate alternate hosts and wild self-sown wheat volunteers
Follow regional surveillance advisories issued by wheat rust monitoring stations
Brown Rust.source: ICAR - IIWBR Karnal Wheat Rust Monitoring Station, Flowerdale
Brown Rust.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Yellow Rust.explanation: Yellow / Stripe Rust (Puccinia striiformis) thrives in cool humid conditions, producing bright lemon-yellow pustules arranged in distinct narrow linear stripes.
symptoms: Small bright yellow to orange-yellow pustules arranged in parallel linear stripes
Lesions resemble narrow yellow ribbons running down the leaf blade and glumes
Chlorotic and necrotic stripes remain after spores discharge; severe shriveling of grains
culturalActions: Inspect cool, shaded, or low-lying field corners where moisture lingers in December-January
Cease overhead sprinkler irrigation during active yellow rust alerts
Report initial focal patches to local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) extension officers
prevention: Sow verified stripe-rust resistant cultivars recommended for sub-montane/plains zones
Avoid growing highly susceptible older varieties
Ensure seed treatment with certified registered fungicides if recommended locally
Yellow Rust.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Powdery Mildew.explanation: Powdery Mildew (Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici) causes fluffy white to gray powdery fungal patches across lower leaves and stems, reducing photosynthetic area.
symptoms: White fluffy powdery fungal colonies on leaf blades, sheaths, and lower stems
Patches enlarge and turn dull gray with tiny black speck-like fruiting bodies (cleistothecia)
Underlying leaf tissue turns chlorotic yellow and desiccates prematurely
culturalActions: Avoid overly dense plant canopies and excessive nitrogenous fertilization
Promote sun penetration and air circulation across the crop canopy
Scout shaded field perimeters adjoining trees or windbreaks
prevention: Sow certified tolerant cultivars with open erect canopy architecture
Follow recommended seed rate to avoid dense crowding
Rotate fields out of susceptible cereals
Powdery Mildew.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Septoria.explanation: Septoria Leaf Blotch (Zymoseptoria tritici) causes irregular tan to brown blotches studded with tiny black pycnidia speckles, progressing from bottom foliage upward.
symptoms: Irregular oval to rectangular tan blotches on leaf blades
Prominent tiny black pinhead-sized dots (pycnidia) embedded inside dead lesions
Extensive blighting of flag leaf under extended rainy overcast spells
culturalActions: Plow under infected crop residues immediately post-harvest
Avoid excessive nitrogen that stimulates dense lower leaf moisture retention
Monitor flag leaf protection carefully from boot stage through grain fill
prevention: Adopt 2-year crop rotation with non-cereal crops (mustard, chickpea, potato)
Use certified clean pathogen-free seed lots
Plant certified resistant varieties suited to irrigated high-yield tracts
Septoria.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: The cotton crop exhibits robust vegetative branching, deep green palmately lobed leaves, intact leaf margins, healthy squares/bolls, and no vascular wilting.
symptoms: Vibrant green leaves with clear venation and absence of crinkling
Uniform square and boll development with no premature shedding
Firm erect main stem and healthy sympodial fruiting branches
culturalActions: Maintain regular furrow or drip irrigation; avoid waterlogging in root zone
Monitor crop weekly using yellow and blue sticky traps for sucking pests
Apply balanced N-P-K with micronutrient foliar spray (Magnesium and Boron) during boll development
prevention: Plant certified Bt cotton hybrids adapted to local rainfed or irrigated conditions
Adopt recommended plant spacing (90 cm × 60 cm or 120 cm × 45 cm)
Maintain clean bunds free of weed hosts (Abutilon, Xanthium)
Healthy.source: ICAR - Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Bacterial Blight.explanation: Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot (Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum) produces distinct angular water-soaked lesions bounded by leaf veinlets.
symptoms: Small angular water-soaked lesions bounded strictly by leaf veins
Lesions turn reddish-brown to black on both leaf surfaces
Black arm symptom on branches and water-soaked dark sunken spots on bolls
culturalActions: Rogue and burn severely infected plant stalks and diseased seedlings
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation that splashes bacterial cells across rows
Clean farm tools with certified disinfectant between operations
prevention: Delint and treat planting seeds with concentrated acid and certified bactericide
Sow certified blight-tolerant cotton hybrids
Destroy cotton stalks post-harvest rather than storing them in field borders
Bacterial Blight.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Curl Virus.explanation: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV) is a devastating begomovirus vectored by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci), producing upward leaf curling, enations, and thickened veins.
symptoms: Upward or downward cupping and curling of leaf margins
Thickening of primary and secondary leaf veins on undersides
Small cup-shaped leaf-like outgrowths (enations) on leaf undersides; severe plant stunting
culturalActions: Install yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre) to track whitefly density
Eradicate weed hosts (Sida, Abutilon, Parthenium) around fields
Rogue and bury severely infected stunt plants during early 60 days of growth
prevention: Plant certified CLCuD-tolerant hybrid varieties recommended for your state
Avoid planting near alternate host crops like okra or tobacco
Spray registered botanical neem formulation (1500 ppm at 3ml/L) to suppress whitefly colonization
Curl Virus.source: ICAR - CICR Regional Station, Sirsa & NCIPM
Curl Virus.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Fusarium Wilt.explanation: Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. vasinfectum) is a soil-borne vascular wilt causing yellowing, drooping, and internal dark vascular ring browning.
symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis and yellowing starting on lower leaves, spreading upward
Sudden wilting and drooping of foliage during hot sunny afternoons
Cutting the lower stem reveals dark brown to black vascular discoloration
culturalActions: Uproot and burn wilted plants with roots to prevent chlamydospore accumulation in soil
Improve field drainage; avoid standing water in heavy black clay soils
Apply Trichoderma viride enriched farmyard manure (2.5 kg Trichoderma in 250 kg FYM/acre)
prevention: Plant certified wilt-resistant cotton cultivars
Enforce a 3 to 4-year crop rotation with non-host crops like sorghum or millets
Avoid using tools from known wilt-infested plots without thorough sanitization
Fusarium Wilt.source: ICAR - Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR)
Fusarium Wilt.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Target Spot.explanation: Target Spot (Corynespora cassiicola) is a foliar fungal pathogen producing large circular lesions with dark brown concentric rings, often causing severe lower canopy defoliation.
symptoms: Circular to irregular brown lesions with prominent concentric target rings
Lesions develop rapidly in the dense lower canopy during humid warm periods
Severe infection causes premature defoliation of lower and middle leaves
culturalActions: Promote canopy air circulation by avoiding excessive plant density and excessive nitrogen
Scout the lower third of the canopy during boll-opening stage
Remove fallen severely infected leaves where practical
prevention: Select varieties with open canopy architecture
Follow recommended row spacing (minimum 90 cm)
Rotate fields out of susceptible host crops
Target Spot.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: The soybean crop displays healthy trifoliate leaves, uniform dark green foliage, vigorous nodulation on roots, and clean pods free of blights or rust spots.
symptoms: Uniform green trifoliate leaves with smooth margins and no yellowing
Vigorous branching with healthy flower clusters and pod setting
Pink active nitrogen-fixing nodules on primary and secondary root system
culturalActions: Maintain adequate soil moisture during flowering and pod development stages
Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium japonicum and PSB before sowing for optimal nodulation
Keep the field weed-free during the first 30-45 critical days
prevention: Sow certified soybean seed with verified germination > 70%
Adopt broad bed furrow (BBF) or ridge-and-furrow planting to drain excess monsoon water
Rotate soybean with wheat, gram, or mustard in rabi season
Healthy.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR), Indore
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Cercospora Leaf Blight.explanation: Cercospora Leaf Blight (Cercospora kikuchii) produces reddish-purple to bronze discoloration on upper canopy foliage exposed to sunlight.
symptoms: Upper canopy leaves develop reddish-purple to bronze leathery appearance
Leaves become thickened, crinkled, and drop prematurely
Purple seed stain visible on harvested soybean seeds
culturalActions: Deep plow crop residues immediately following harvest to bury fungal inocula
Avoid using purple-stained seeds from diseased plots for subsequent sowing
Ensure balanced balanced potassium fertilization
prevention: Sow certified tolerant varieties recommended by IISR Indore
Treat seeds prior to sowing with certified biological Trichoderma inoculants
Practice crop rotation with non-leguminous cereals
Cercospora Leaf Blight.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Frogeye Leaf Spot.explanation: Frogeye Leaf Spot (Cercospora sojina) is characterized by small circular to angular spots with gray to tan centers surrounded by narrow dark reddish-brown borders.
symptoms: Small circular to angular lesions with tan or gray centers and reddish-brown borders
Spots resemble a frog's eye, primarily on the upper surface of leaves
Lesions may coalesce to form large blighted areas, leading to premature leaf drop
culturalActions: Inspect canopy regularly during warm, humid monsoon spells
Incorporate stubble and residue into the soil post-harvest
Avoid continuous monocropping of soybean on infected parcels
prevention: Plant certified resistant soybean cultivars
Use certified pathogen-free seeds tested for seed-borne fungal pathogens
Maintain 2-year crop rotation with maize or sorghum
Frogeye Leaf Spot.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Soybean Research (IISR)
Frogeye Leaf Spot.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Rust.explanation: Soybean Rust (Phakopsora pachyrhizi) is an aggressive foliar fungal disease producing tiny chlorotic flecks that rapidly develop into raised brown pustules on leaf undersides.
symptoms: Tiny chlorotic flecks developing into small raised reddish-brown pustules on leaf undersides
Spotted leaves turn yellow, appear scorched, and defoliate rapidly within days
Premature defoliation drastically curtails pod filling and yield
culturalActions: Conduct intense scouting on lower leaves starting at flowering stage in high-risk zones
Report early focal outbreaks to local district agricultural officers
Ensure adequate row spacing to facilitate air movement
prevention: Sow early-maturing certified varieties to escape late-season spore showers
Monitor regional rust alerts published by ICAR-IISR Indore
Apply recommended preventive bio-formulations upon first detection in district
Rust.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Yellow Mosaic.explanation: Soybean Yellow Mosaic Virus is a begomovirus vectored by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci), creating striking alternating yellow and green mosaic patterns on foliage.
symptoms: Bright yellow mosaic patches interspersed with green areas on leaf blades
Affected leaves become puckered, smaller in size, and leathery
Flowering is severely delayed and pods produced are few, small, and contain shriveled seeds
culturalActions: Install yellow sticky traps (15 traps/acre) uniformly across the field to capture whiteflies
Rogue and destroy infected seedlings in the first 30 days of crop growth
Maintain weed-free field borders to eliminate alternate hosts (Croton, Parthenium)
prevention: Sow certified YMV-resistant cultivars (e.g., JS 20-34, JS 20-29, NRC 86 where recommended)
Treat seeds prior to sowing with certified registered seed protectants
Avoid staggered sowing dates across neighboring plots
Yellow Mosaic.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: The sugarcane crop exhibits robust stalk development, vibrant green leaf blades with prominent clean midribs, uniform tillering, and zero signs of red rot or mosaic streaks.
symptoms: Uniform deep green leaf lamina with intact serrated margins
Clean central midrib with no reddish discoloration or pith breakdown
Sturdy erect cane stalks with healthy node and internode elongation
culturalActions: Maintain scheduled nitrogen and potassium fertigation matching grand growth period
Ensure effective drainage in furrows to prevent standing water during monsoon
Conduct routine bi-weekly leaf inspections and trash mulching
prevention: Use certified disease-free 2-budded or 3-budded setts from registered nurseries
Practice proper crop rotation with leguminous green manure (sunnhemp / dhaincha)
Adopt wider row spacing (120-150 cm) for single/paired row planting
Healthy.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Sugarcane Research (IISR), Lucknow & SBI Coimbatore
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Red Rot.explanation: Red Rot (Colletotrichum falcatum) is the most destructive disease of sugarcane in India, causing internal stalk reddening, white transverse cross-patches, and sudden stool drying.
symptoms: Elongated reddish lesions on the upper leaf midrib
Third and fourth leaves wither and turn yellow-red from tips downward
Splitting the cane stalk reveals dark red internal tissues with distinctive white cross-bands and alcoholic odor
culturalActions: Immediately uproot and burn all affected clumps along with root systems
Do not ratoon fields infected with red rot; prepare land for crop rotation
Avoid flowing irrigation water from infected blocks into healthy cane blocks
prevention: Plant certified red-rot resistant varieties recommended for your zone (e.g., Co 86032, Co 0238 where suitable)
Treat seed setts with moist hot air therapy (MHAT at 54°C for 2.5 hours) or biological Trichoderma soak
Follow a strict 2 to 3-year crop rotation with paddy, maize, or legumes
Red Rot.source: ICAR - Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Coimbatore & IISR Lucknow
Red Rot.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Rust.explanation: Sugarcane Rust (Puccinia melanocephala) produces small elongated chlorotic spots that erupt into reddish-brown powdery pustules along leaf blades.
symptoms: Small yellowish elongated spots developing into reddish-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture releasing masses of orange-brown urediniospores
Premature drying and scorching of leaves under heavy infestation
culturalActions: Remove lower dry senescent leaves (detrashing) to enhance airflow and reduce humidity
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization that stimulates overly succulent foliage
Scout fields weekly during warm humid weather
prevention: Cultivate certified rust-resistant sugarcane varieties
Maintain optimal plant density and row spacing to ensure good canopy ventilation
Adopt drip fertigation to minimize canopy wetting
Rust.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Mosaic.explanation: Sugarcane Mosaic Virus (SCMV) causes contrasting light green or yellow chlorotic streaks across leaf blades, reducing photosynthesis and stalk weight.
symptoms: Contrasting light green or yellow chlorotic streaks on green leaf lamina
Mottled pattern more prominent on young expanding leaves
Stunted stool growth and reduced cane diameter in severe infections
culturalActions: Rogue out and destroy infected young plants early in the season
Monitor and control aphid vectors using sticky traps and field sanitation
Disinfect harvesting knives between fields
prevention: Plant virus-free tissue culture seed setts
Keep field borders clean of wild grassy weeds that host SCMV
Plant certified disease-free nursery seed cane
Mosaic.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Yellow Disease.explanation: Sugarcane Yellow Leaf Disease (SCYLV) causes intense yellowing of the leaf midrib and lamina, severely impairing sucrose accumulation and yield.
symptoms: Bright yellowing of the lower leaf midrib on the 3rd to 6th leaves
Yellowing spreading sideways into the leaf lamina
Stalk shortening, apical leaf bunching, and premature senescence in advanced stages
culturalActions: Remove and burn symptomatic stools to curb aphid-mediated transmission
Apply balanced N-P-K nutrients to support plant immunity
Maintain clean field borders free of alternate host grasses
prevention: Use SCYLV-certified seed material from nursery plots
Practice strict weed control along field margins
Adopt tissue-culture derived certified planting materials
Yellow Disease.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: The chickpea (gram) crop shows vigorous branching, uniform pinnate green leaflets, healthy root system with active pink nodules, and clean pods free of wilt or blight.
symptoms: Uniform green pinnate leaflets with intact glandular hairs
Healthy erect bushy branching with active flower buds and pod filling
Healthy root system with prominent nitrogen-fixing Rhizobium nodules
culturalActions: Provide light irrigation at pre-flowering and pod-development stages if winter rainfall is absent
Inoculate seeds with Mesorhizobium ciceri and PSB culture before sowing
Maintain proper weed management during the first 30-40 days
prevention: Sow certified disease-resistant chickpea varieties (e.g., JG-11, JAKI 9218, Digvijay)
Adopt broad bed and furrow (BBF) or ridge planting to prevent waterlogging
Rotate chickpea with sorghum, pearl millet, or maize in kharif season
Healthy.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Ascochyta Blight.explanation: Ascochyta Blight (Ascochyta rabiei) is an aggressive foliar fungal disease forming circular necrotic lesions with concentric rings of tiny black pycnidia on leaves, stems, and pods.
symptoms: Circular to elongated necrotic lesions on leaves, stems, and pods
Concentric rings of tiny black pinhead-like fruiting bodies (pycnidia) inside lesions
Stem girdling causing branches to snap and break over easily in the wind
culturalActions: Collect and burn crop debris immediately following harvest to destroy perithecia
Avoid working in fields when morning dew or rain makes foliage wet
Maintain wide row spacing to allow sunlight penetration
prevention: Sow certified Ascochyta-resistant cultivars recommended by IIPR Kanpur
Treat seed with certified biological or registered seed-dressing fungicides
Enforce 3-year crop rotation with non-leguminous cereals
Ascochyta Blight.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Fusarium Wilt.explanation: Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. ciceris) is a destructive soil-borne vascular wilt causing sudden drooping of leaves and internal dark vascular browning of the root/stem.
symptoms: Drooping of petioles and rachis within 3-4 weeks after sowing or at flowering stage
Foliage turns dull pale green before drying completely without yellowing
Splitting the taproot longitudinally reveals dark brown to black internal vascular discoloration
culturalActions: Uproot and burn wilted plants to prevent chlamydospore proliferation in the soil
Deep summer plowing to expose resting spores to hot summer sun
Apply Trichoderma viride enriched compost (5 kg Trichoderma in 500 kg FYM/ha) during final land preparation
prevention: Sow certified wilt-resistant chickpea varieties (e.g. JG-14, JG-315, KWR-108)
Treat seeds prior to sowing with Trichoderma harzianum (4-5 g/kg seed)
Practice multi-year crop rotation with wheat, mustard, or sorghum
Fusarium Wilt.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR) & ICRISAT
Fusarium Wilt.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Dry Root Rot.explanation: Dry Root Rot (Rhizoctonia bataticola / Macrophomina phaseolina) is a devastating fungal root rot emerging under moisture stress and high temperatures (>30°C).
symptoms: Whole plant withers and dries up suddenly; leaves turn yellowish-gray or straw-colored
Taproot becomes brittle, blackened, completely dry, and devoid of secondary rootlets
Splitting the bark reveals dark ash-gray fungal sclerotial bodies embedded in the wood
culturalActions: Provide light irrigation during pod development to relieve severe drought stress
Avoid water stress and high soil temperature by applying light organic straw mulch
Maintain soil organic matter by adding compost or well-decomposed FYM
prevention: Sow certified tolerant varieties adapted to rainfed conditions
Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride or certified bio-fungicide formulations
Schedule sowing early to ensure pod filling completes before severe spring heat
Dry Root Rot.source: ICAR - IIPR Kanpur & ICRISAT Pulses Program
Dry Root Rot.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Stunt Virus.explanation: Chickpea Stunt Disease is caused by luteoviruses transmitted by aphids (Aphis craccivora), causing shortened internodes, bushy appearance, and reddish-brown foliage.
symptoms: Severe shortening of internodes giving the plant a distinctive stunted bushy appearance
Leaflets turn yellow-brown, orange, or reddish-brown and become thickened and brittle
Phloem browning visible as a dark ring when the collar region is sliced transversely
culturalActions: Rogue and destroy stunted plants in the early vegetative stage
Monitor and control aphid populations using yellow sticky traps
Maintain clean bunds free of weed hosts (Medicago, Melilotus)
prevention: Sow certified tolerant chickpea cultivars
Adopt optimum plant density to avoid sparse patchy stands that attract aphid vectors
Spray registered botanical neem extract (Azadirachtin 1500 ppm at 3ml/L) if aphid colonies form
Stunt Virus.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: Onion foliage exhibits healthy erect tubular leaves with uniform bluish-green waxy sheen, vigorous bulb swelling, and no neck rotting or foliar flecking.
symptoms: Erect tubular leaves with smooth waxy cuticle
Absence of purple lesions, sunken spots, or downy mold
Firm, tight neck and uniform bulb expansion
culturalActions: Maintain raised bed planting to prevent water stagnation around bulb necks
Cease irrigation 10-15 days prior to harvesting to promote neck closure and curing
Ensure balanced potash application to enhance storage keeping quality
prevention: Use certified seeds of adapted varieties (Bhima Super, Bhima Red, Bhima Kiran)
Follow crop rotation with non-allium crops like maize, sugarcane, or soybean
Dip seedlings in Trichoderma viride suspension before transplanting
Healthy.source: ICAR - Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR), Rajgurunagar, Pune
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Purple Blotch.explanation: Purple Blotch (Alternaria porri) is a serious fungal disease prevalent in Maharashtra during warm humid weather, producing sunken purple-centered lesions on leaves and seed stalks.
symptoms: Small water-soaked lesions that enlarge into sunken elliptic spots with purplish-brown centers
Concentric dark and light zones surrounded by a chlorotic yellow halo
Leaves break over at the point of lesion development and wither
culturalActions: Rogue out severely spotted foliage and avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation
Destroy all volunteer allium weeds and field trash post-harvest
Provide wide row spacing for canopy ventilation
prevention: Apply certified seed treatment using thiram or carbendazim at 2g/kg seed
Spray bio-fungicide Pseudomonas fluorescens at 5g/L at first appearance of spots
Follow 3-year crop rotation avoiding garlic and leeks
Purple Blotch.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Stemphylium Blight.explanation: Stemphylium Leaf Blight (Stemphylium vesicarium) causes yellow-to-pale-orange oval flecks on outer leaves that coalesce into severe foliar blighting.
symptoms: Small yellowish-white flecks that rapidly expand into elongated spindle-shaped spots
Lesions turn olive-brown to dark brown as fungal spores develop
Complete drying of tops resulting in premature defoliation and undersized bulbs
culturalActions: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which produces soft, susceptible succulent foliage
Provide deep drainage channels to prevent soil saturation
Collect and burn infected onion tops following harvest
prevention: Adopt wider plant spacing (15 cm x 10 cm) on raised beds
Foliar spray of neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) as preventive measure
Rotate with pulses or cereals
Stemphylium Blight.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Basal Rot.explanation: Fusarium Basal Rot (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cepae) attacks the onion root plate and bulb base, causing root dieback, water-soaked brown decay, and storage rot.
symptoms: Yellowing and progressive backward dieback of leaves starting from tips
Roots rot, turn dark brown to pinkish, and detach easily from the stem plate
Basal portion of the bulb softens and decays with whitish mycelial growth
culturalActions: Carefully sort and discard all wounded, bruised, or discolored bulbs before storage
Ensure prompt field curing under well-ventilated sheds
Avoid cultivating onion in fields with known basal rot history
prevention: Soil application of Trichoderma harzianum enriched FYM (2.5 kg/ton) prior to transplanting
Solarize nursery beds with clear polythene sheets during summer months
Follow a strict 4-5 year crop rotation with non-host graminaceous crops
Basal Rot.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Downy Mildew.explanation: Downy Mildew (Peronospora destructor) is a severe fungal disease of onion foliage causing pale oval lesions with grayish-violet downy growth, leading to leaf collapse.
symptoms: Pale elongated yellowish spots on older leaves
Purplish-gray downy fungal fuzz on spots during cool dewy mornings
Leaf tips withering, twisting downward, and collapsing prematurely
culturalActions: Ensure wide ridge spacing to accelerate foliar morning drying
Destroy cull piles and volunteer onion plants around fields
Avoid working in fields while leaves are wet with morning dew
prevention: Practice a 3-year crop rotation avoiding allium crops
Use certified disease-free onion sets/seedlings
Orient rows parallel to prevailing winds to reduce canopy humidity
Downy Mildew.source: ICAR - Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR), Rajgurunagar, Pune
Downy Mildew.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: Pigeon Pea (Tur/Arhar) exhibits vigorous vegetative branching, healthy trifoliate leaves, active nodulation on roots, and prolific flowering without wilting or mosaic mottle.
symptoms: Uniform green trifoliate foliage with intact leaflets
Sturdy erect branches with prolific bud and flower formation
Healthy root system with pink active nitrogen-fixing nodules
culturalActions: Intercrop with soybean, sorghum, or pearl millet (1:2 ratio) to reduce pest incidence
Ensure field surface drainage during high monsoon downpours
Nip apical terminal shoots at 45 days to stimulate prolific lateral branching
prevention: Inoculate seeds with certified Rhizobium and Trichoderma cultures prior to sowing
Plant wilt-resistant cultivars (BSMR 736, BDN 711, Maruti ICP 8863)
Deep summer plowing to expose resting pathogen pupae and spores to solar heat
Healthy.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR) & VNMKV Parbhani
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Fusarium Wilt.explanation: Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium udum) is the most destructive soil-borne vascular wilt disease of pigeon pea in Maharashtra, causing sudden flaccidity and xylem browning.
symptoms: Gradual or sudden wilting of foliage, often progressing from one side of the plant
Leaves turn dull green, droop, yellow, and dry up while remaining attached to branches
Dark purple-to-black vascular browning visible beneath the bark along the lower stem
culturalActions: Immediately rogue and burn wilted plants to prevent micro-conidial buildup in soil
Do not cultivate ratoon crops in infested fields
Avoid flood irrigation that washes fungal spores across field rows
prevention: Grow certified wilt-resistant varieties (Asha, BSMR 736, BSMR 853)
Apply Trichoderma viride enriched farmyard manure at 5 kg/ha in seed furrows
Practice 3-year crop rotation with sorghum or tobacco which breaks the disease cycle
Fusarium Wilt.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Sterility Mosaic Disease.explanation: Sterility Mosaic Disease (SMD) - known as 'Green Plague' of Tur - is caused by Pigeonpea Sterility Mosaic Virus transmitted by the eriophyid mite (Aceria cajani).
symptoms: Severe mosaic mottling with alternating light green and dark green leaf patches
Severe reduction in leaflet size and bushy bunchy appearance due to shortened internodes
Complete cessation of reproductive flowering, rendering the plant completely sterile
culturalActions: Rogue out and destroy infected plants at early vegetative stage
Eradicate wild perennial pigeon pea and volunteer plants along field borders
Monitor for eriophyid mite vectors on lower leaf surfaces
prevention: Cultivate SMD-resistant varieties such as BSMR 736, BDN 2, or ICPL 87119 (Asha)
Spray registered acaricide or wettable sulfur (3g/L) during early vegetative flush if mites appear
Maintain weed-free field boundaries
Sterility Mosaic Disease.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: Groundnut (Bhuimug) displays healthy tetrafoliate leaves with vibrant green coloration, prostrate or bunch canopy vigor, clean stems, and prolific pegging into soil.
symptoms: Bright green 4-leaflet leaves with zero necrotic spots or rust pustules
Abundant yellow flower bloom and healthy subterranean gynophore peg entry
Sturdy stems free of collar rot or white fungal mycelium
culturalActions: Keep soil loose and friable around plant base through light hoeing prior to pegging
Maintain optimal soil moisture during flowering and pod development stages
Provide gypsum application (400-500 kg/ha) at 40-45 days for optimal shell development
prevention: Treat seeds with Trichoderma viride (4 g/kg seed) and certified Rhizobium culture
Grow high-yielding adapted cultivars (TAG 24, TG 37A, Phule Unnati, JL 24)
Rotate with cereals (pearl millet, sorghum, maize) every alternate season
Healthy.source: ICAR - Directorate of Groundnut Research (DGR) Junagadh & MPKV Rahuri
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Tikka Leaf Spot.explanation: Tikka disease (Cercospora arachidicola / Cercosporidium personatum) causes widespread circular necrotic spotting and premature defoliation across groundnut fields in Maharashtra.
symptoms: Early leaf spots: Circular reddish-brown to dark brown with a distinct yellow halo
Late leaf spots: Circular blackish spots without halo, concentrated on the lower leaf surface
Premature shedding of foliage leaving bare stems and resulting in small shriveled pods
culturalActions: Remove and burn plant debris and volunteer groundnut plants after harvest
Avoid overhead irrigation which splashes spores from lower to upper canopy
Adopt optimum row spacing (30 cm x 10 cm) to facilitate canopy aeration
prevention: Foliar spray of 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) at early onset of disease
Seed treatment with captan or thiram at 3g/kg seed
Spray registered bio-protective formulations as recommended by local Krishi Vigyan Kendra
Tikka Leaf Spot.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Rust.explanation: Groundnut Rust (Puccinia arachidis) produces numerous small orange-to-brown pustules on the lower leaf surfaces, causing leaves to curl and dry up.
symptoms: Small, circular, reddish-orange pustules predominantly on lower leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture releasing masses of powdery rust-colored urediniospores
Leaves curl, turn brown, dry up, and remain attached to stems without defoliating
culturalActions: Intercrop with pigeon pea or pearl millet to slow airborne spore dispersal
Destroy all wild Arachis host species in field margins
Ensure field is cleared of all crop residues following harvest
prevention: Grow rust-tolerant groundnut cultivars (Phule Bharati, GPBD 4)
Spray wettable sulfur (3g/L) at 10-15 day intervals upon initial symptom detection
Follow crop rotation with non-leguminous cereals
Rust.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: Pomegranate (Dalimb - Bhagwa GI) exhibits glossy green lanceolate foliage, strong canes, abundant bright red flower buds, and clean developing fruit with intact calyxes.
symptoms: Glossy, leathery oblong foliage with vibrant green pigmentation
Sturdy canes without water-soaked lesions or bacterial weeping
Smooth, unblemished fruit rind with characteristic deep red color
culturalActions: Prune dead, criss-crossed, and diseased twigs cleanly and paste cuts with copper oxychloride
Regulate irrigation using drip emitters positioned outside the tree canopy line
Follow recommended bahar treatment (Ambe, Hasta, or Mrig) adapted to regional water availability
prevention: Plant certified tissue-cultured or disease-free air-layered Bhagwa saplings
Spray biostimulants and bio-agents (Pseudomonas fluorescens) as preventive barriers
Sterilize secateurs and pruning shears with sodium hypochlorite between trees
Healthy.source: ICAR - National Research Centre on Pomegranate (NRCP), Solapur
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Bacterial Blight.explanation: Bacterial Blight or 'Telya / Oily Spot' (Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. punicae) is the most destructive disease of pomegranate in Solapur and Maharashtra, producing greasy black lesions and fruit cracking.
symptoms: Small water-soaked, translucent spots on leaves that turn dark brown to black and oily
Leaves turn yellow, wither, and prematurely drop, causing severe canopy thinning
Distinctive brown-to-black L-shaped or Y-shaped cracks with oozing bacterial exudate on fruits
culturalActions: Strictly prune and burn all blighted twigs 5 cm below the infected zone, sterilizing shears
Apply Bordeaux paste (10%) on main trunk and major branch crotches
Defoliate and destroy fallen leaves completely during rest period
prevention: Spray certified bactericide-copper formulations (Streptocycline 0.5g/L + Copper Oxychloride 2.5g/L) under extension supervision
Avoid overhead irrigation or high nitrogen fertigation during humid rainy periods
Quarantine planting material and source exclusively from certified blight-free nurseries
Bacterial Blight.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Anthracnose.explanation: Pomegranate Anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) causes dark brown circular spots with concentric rings on leaves and small sunken spots on ripening fruit.
symptoms: Circular to angular brown necrotic spots with yellow halos on leaves
Sunken dark brown to black spots on fruit rind, expanding into leathery lesions
Premature leaf yellowing and unmarketable blemished fruit
culturalActions: Prune internal canopy to allow maximum sunlight penetration and rapid foliage drying
Collect and bury fallen infected fruit and mummified rinds
Avoid mechanical wounding of fruit rind during bagging or spraying
prevention: Preventive spray of copper hydroxide or mancozeb at 2.5g/L during cloudy rainy days
Maintain balanced potassium and micronutrient nutrition
Apply botanical neem oil (3ml/L) as protective coating
Anthracnose.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: Grapevine (Draksha) exhibits vigorous trellised cordons, vibrant green palmate foliage, healthy tendrils, and uniform berry clusters without fungal powder or mildew patches.
symptoms: Uniform green palmate leaves with sharp defined serrations
Firm green berries with natural waxy bloom on skin
Strong shoots and canes free of cankers or necrotic cracking
culturalActions: Practice systematic canopy thinning and sub-shoot pinching to optimize airflow and sunlight
Maintain drip irrigation and schedule canopy rest pruning according to October pruning calendar
Ensure balanced gibberellic acid (GA3) and bio-stimulant fertigation for uniform berry spacing
prevention: Use certified disease-free rootstocks (e.g., Dog Ridge, 110R)
Apply Trichoderma viride enriched compost around the root zone
Erect protective weather-monitoring stations for early microclimate disease warning
Healthy.source: ICAR - National Research Centre for Grapes (NRCG), Pune
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Downy Mildew.explanation: Downy Mildew (Plasmopara viticola) is the most destructive disease of grapevines in Nashik and Sangli, producing translucent 'oil spots' on leaf uppers and white cottony down beneath.
symptoms: Yellowish, oily translucent spots ('oil spots') on the upper leaf surface
Dense white downy cottony fungal growth on the corresponding lower surface in high humidity
Browning, drying, and dropping of flower clusters and young infected berries
culturalActions: Prune lower canopy leaves within 30 cm of soil level to prevent ground-splash infection
Avoid overhead irrigation; maintain drip lines strictly along the vine rows
Remove and burn fallen infected leaves and dried mummified berry bunches
prevention: Spray Bordeaux mixture (1%) or copper oxychloride as preventive shield before rains
Follow NRCG weather-based advisory bulletin for systemic fungicide timing
Apply potassium phosphonate at 3ml/L as systemic disease inducer
Downy Mildew.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Powdery Mildew.explanation: Powdery Mildew (Erysiphe necator) coats leaves, shoots, and developing berries with an ash-grey powdery growth, causing berry cracking and unmarketable fruit.
symptoms: Ash-gray to white powdery fungal patches on upper and lower leaf surfaces
Young leaves become distorted, curled upwards, and dwarfed
Berries develop a webbed russeting, fail to expand, and crack open, exposing seeds
culturalActions: Ensure good canopy aeration by de-shooting and shoot positioning on bower/trellis
Avoid excessive application of vegetative nitrogen fertilizers
Prune infected flag shoots during winter dormancy
prevention: Dust or spray sulfur (wettable sulfur at 2g/L) during cool morning hours
Apply bio-protective ampelomyces or Bacillus subtilis cultures
Rotate with registered fungicides having different modes of action to manage resistance
Powdery Mildew.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Black Rot.explanation: Black Rot (Guignardia bidwellii) is a destructive fungal disease causing small circular reddish-brown spots on grape foliage and shriveled black mummified berries.
symptoms: Small circular reddish-brown leaf spots with dark margins
Tiny black fruiting bodies (pycnidia) arranged in rings inside spots
Berry shriveling into hard black wrinkled mummies
culturalActions: Prune and destroy infected canes, mummies, and leaf litter during dormant season
Maintain canopy trellising for optimal air circulation and rapid sun drying
Avoid excessive canopy shading in vineyard rows
prevention: Follow regular winter dormant sanitation sprays
Ensure timely canopy management before monsoon rains
Plant less susceptible rootstocks and cultivars
Black Rot.source: ICAR - National Research Centre for Grapes (NRCG), Pune
Black Rot.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Esca (Black Measles).explanation: Esca or Black Measles (complex of Phaeomoniella chlamydospora and Phaeoacremonium minimum) is a vascular trunk disease causing distinctive 'tiger-stripe' leaf chlorosis and berry spotting.
symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' chlorotic and necrotic patterns between leaf veins
Dark purple to brown spots (measles) on berry skins
Apoplexy or sudden summer wilting of entire vines
culturalActions: Disinfect pruning shears with 10% sodium hypochlorite between vine cuts
Seal large pruning wounds with protective biological or wound paste
Remove and burn severely infected dead vine wood
prevention: Use certified disease-free rootstock and scion wood
Avoid pruning during damp, foggy, or rainy days when fungal spores disperse
Maintain balanced vine nutrition and avoid water stress
Esca (Black Measles).source: ICAR - National Research Centre for Grapes (NRCG), Pune
Esca (Black Measles).pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Leaf Blight (Isariopsis).explanation: Isariopsis Leaf Blight (Pseudocercospora vitis) is a foliar fungal disease causing angular to irregular brown necrotic spots on grape leaves, leading to premature defoliation.
symptoms: Irregular angular dark brown lesions on the upper leaf blade
Olive-brown velvety fungal sporulation on lesion undersides in humid weather
Premature drying and drop of older foliage
culturalActions: Strip lower senescent leaves to enhance under-canopy ventilation
Collect and compost fallen blighted leaves to reduce overwintering inocula
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation
prevention: Maintain proper shoot spacing on trellis bower systems
Apply balanced N-P-K fertilizer to prevent lush weak foliage
Inspect vineyard rows bi-weekly during post-monsoon humid flushes
Leaf Blight (Isariopsis).source: ICAR - National Research Centre for Grapes (NRCG), Pune
Leaf Blight (Isariopsis).pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: Banana (Keli) exhibits wide, upright emerald-green leaf laminas with intact midribs, sturdy pseudostem girth, and clean, vigorous hanging fruit bunches without sigatoka streaking.
symptoms: Vibrant green wide paddle-shaped leaf blades with uniform parallel venation
Firm pseudostem without vascular discoloration or gummy exudation
Healthy emergent heart and uniform fingers on hanging bunch
culturalActions: De-sucker regularly, maintaining only one follower sucker per mother plant
Bag fruit bunches with non-woven polypropylene sleeves to protect against sunburn and insect pests
Ensure effective surface drainage trenches to prevent waterlogging during monsoon
prevention: Plant certified disease-free tissue-cultured plantlets (Grand Naine / Robusta)
Solarize and treat pits with Trichoderma and neem cake (250g/pit) before planting
Maintain clean field sanitation and eradicate weeds
Healthy.source: ICAR - National Research Centre for Banana (NRCB) & Dr. PDKV Akola
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Sigatoka Leaf Spot.explanation: Yellow and Black Sigatoka (Pseudocercospora musae / fijiensis) causes severe foliar necrosis, reducing photosynthetic leaf area and leading to premature fruit ripening.
symptoms: Small yellowish or chlorotic streaks parallel to leaf veins
Streaks expand into spindle-shaped brown-to-black lesions with grayish-white centers
Coalescence of lesions causes extensive leaf blighting, premature leaf collapse, and small fingers
culturalActions: De-leaf and chop severely infected leaves, burying them face down or mulching between rows
Maintain wide planting geometry (1.8m x 1.8m) to facilitate breeze and canopy drying
Avoid sprinkler or overhead wetting
prevention: Foliar spray of mineral oil or neem oil (10ml/L) emulsified with detergent as preventive coating
Apply copper-based fungicides at onset of monsoon rains
Maintain optimal plant nutrition with balanced potassium and silica fertigation
Sigatoka Leaf Spot.source: ICAR - NRCB Trichy & Dr. PDKV Akola
