Panama Wilt.explanation: Panama Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense) is a devastating vascular disease causing yellowing of lower leaves, skirt-like drooping, and internal pseudostem browning.
symptoms: Progressive yellowing of lower older leaves from petiole upwards
Leaves buckle at the petiole base and hang down skirt-like around the pseudostem
Reddish-brown to dark purple vascular discoloration visible inside the split pseudostem
culturalActions: Uproot and burn infected plants along with root corms; drench pit with lime
Do not use suckers from infected plantations for propagation
Strictly avoid moving contaminated soil or irrigation water to healthy plots
prevention: Grow resistant or tolerant Cavendish cultivars (Grand Naine)
Incorporate bio-agent Trichoderma viride with farmyard manure (2 kg/plant) at pit preparation
Crop rotation with sugarcane or paddy in wet fields to suppress Fusarium chlamydospores
Panama Wilt.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: Mango (Alphonso / Hapus GI) foliage exhibits dark green leathery lanceolate leaves, vigorous terminal flushes, healthy panicle blossoms, and clean developing fruitlets.
symptoms: Deep green glossy lanceolate leaves without spotting or leaf roll
Sturdy branches with healthy terminal buds free of dieback
Abundant clean flowering panicles with high fruit set
culturalActions: Prune deadwood, criss-cross branches, and water shoots after harvesting in June
Paste main tree trunks with Bordeaux paste (10%) to protect against gummosis and borers
Withhold irrigation 2-3 months prior to flowering to encourage uniform vegetative bud dormancy
prevention: Spray neem oil (3ml/L) during new vegetative leaf flushes to repel hopper vectors
Apply paclobutrazol (Cultar) strictly according to tree canopy diameter and DBSKKV recommendations
Maintain clean orchard floor free of leaf litter
Healthy.source: ICAR - Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture (CISH) & DBSKKV Dapoli
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Anthracnose.explanation: Mango Anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) causes leaf spotting, panicle blight, and post-harvest tear-drop black rot on fruit skins across coastal Konkan orchards.
symptoms: Small, dark brown, circular to angular spots with raised margins on young leaves
Blighting of blossom panicles causing blossom drop and failure of fruit set
Sunken, dark brown to black circular lesions on ripening fruit developing characteristic tear-stain streaks
culturalActions: Prune and destroy all blighted twigs and dried mummified panicles post-harvest
Thin dense canopy branches to improve interior sunlight and aeration
Submerge harvested fruits in hot water (52°C) for 10 minutes for post-harvest decay control
prevention: Pre-blossom spray of Copper Oxychloride (2.5g/L) or Carbendazim (1g/L)
Repeat protective spray during fruitlet development stage (marble size)
Avoid overhead irrigation during flowering and fruit ripening
Anthracnose.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Powdery Mildew.explanation: Mango Powdery Mildew (Oidium mangiferae) attacks tender panicles, leaves, and fruitlets, coating them with a white powdery fungal bloom and causing total flower drop.
symptoms: White powdery superficial fungal patches on inflorescence panicles and young leaves
Infected panicles turn brown, dry up, and shatter without fruit set
Tender leaves curl, exhibit distorted margins, and drop prematurely
culturalActions: Prune overcrowded shoots to ensure thorough penetration of spray solutions
Collect and burn fallen inflorescences and blighted leaf litter
Keep orchard floor cleanly disked during spring months
prevention: First preventive spray of wettable sulfur (2g/L) at flower panicle emergence
Second spray of systemic fungicide (dinocap or hexaconazole) during full bloom
Spray during calm early morning or late afternoon hours
Powdery Mildew.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: Nagpur Mandarin Orange (Santra GI) displays healthy dark-green leathery leaves, sturdy green shoots with short thorns, clean fragrant white blossoms, and smooth green/golden fruit.
symptoms: Vibrant dark green foliage with smooth intact margins and glossy cuticle
Sturdy branches without gummy gum-weeping bark or twig dieback
Smooth, unblemished fruit rind with tight attachment
culturalActions: Follow standard bahar regulation (Ambe Bahar or Mrig Bahar) based on soil depth and water supply
Paint tree trunks up to 60 cm from ground level with Bordeaux paste twice annually (May and October)
Ensure basin or ring irrigation system that keeps water from directly touching the trunk bark
prevention: Use certified disease-free budded saplings on resistant rootstocks (Rangpur Lime, Rough Lemon)
Apply Trichoderma harzianum enriched neem cake around the root drip line
Maintain optimal micronutrient spraying (Zinc, Iron, Manganese) during active flush stages
Healthy.source: ICAR - Central Citrus Research Institute (CCRI), Nagpur
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Citrus Canker.explanation: Citrus Canker (Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri) is an endemic bacterial disease causing raised, corky, crater-like lesions surrounded by yellow halos on leaves, twigs, and fruit.
symptoms: Small, round, blister-like raised corky lesions on both leaf surfaces
Corky lesions develop rough, crater-like centers surrounded by prominent oily yellow halos
Crater-like rough scabby brown spots on fruit rind, reducing commercial market value
culturalActions: Prune and burn cankered twigs before onset of monsoon rains
Erect windbreaks (Casuarina, Shevri) around orchards to reduce wind-driven rain transmission
Sterilize pruning equipment between trees with 1% sodium hypochlorite
prevention: Foliar spray of Streptocycline (1g/10L) + Copper Oxychloride (25g/10L) at vegetative flush
Control leaf miner (Phyllocnistis citrella) whose feeding galleries allow bacterial entry
Plant certified disease-free nursery stock from government accredited nurseries
Citrus Canker.source: ICAR - CCRI Nagpur & Dr. PDKV Akola
Citrus Canker.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Phytophthora Gummosis.explanation: Phytophthora Foot Rot and Gummosis (Phytophthora nicotianae / citrophthora) attacks tree collars and root systems, causing bark cracking, profuse gum oozing, and branch dieback.
symptoms: Dark, water-soaked patches on the bark near the soil line that crack and ooze copious amber-colored gum
Bark rots, dries, and strips away longitudinally in shredded strips, girdling the trunk
Yellowing of foliage veins followed by sudden leaf drop and staghead twig dieback
culturalActions: Scrape infected dead bark cleanly down to healthy wood and paste with Bordeaux paste
Form high mounds or ridges around tree bases to ensure water drains away from trunks
Avoid deep soil tilling near trunks that could sever feeder roots
prevention: Bud scions high on the rootstock (at least 25-30 cm above ground level)
Drench soil basin with Fosetyl-Al (2.5g/L) or Metalaxyl-Mancozeb (2g/L) before monsoon
Use Phytophthora-tolerant rootstocks (Rangpur Lime, Alemow)
Phytophthora Gummosis.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: Sorghum (Jowar - Maldandi) shows robust erect stalks, broad arching green leaves with white midribs, strong prop roots, and dense compact grain-bearing panicles.
symptoms: Clean green leaves with healthy white midrib and intact margins
Sturdy thick stalk with healthy prop/brace roots at lower nodes
Well-filled, uniform cream/white grain head without mold or smutting
culturalActions: Follow timely sowing in Rabi (mid-September to first week of October) for optimal Maldandi grain filling
Ensure proper weed control during the first 30 days of seedling establishment
Intercrop with pulses like pigeon pea or chickpea to improve soil fertility and reduce insect pressure
prevention: Use certified seed of high-yielding adapted cultivars (M 35-1 / Maldandi, Phule Yashodha, CSV 22)
Treat seeds with Azotobacter and PSB biofertilizers (250g/10kg seed) before sowing
Deep summer plowing to eliminate stubbles harboring charcoal rot and shoot fly pupae
Healthy.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Millets Research (IIMR) & MPKV Rahuri
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Grain Mold.explanation: Grain Mold complex (Fusarium, Curvularia, Phoma) infects developing sorghum grains during humid wet weather at heading, causing black/pink discoloration and loss of seed viability.
symptoms: Floret and grain discoloration ranging from pink, white, orange to velvety black
Grains become soft, chalky, lightweight, and crumble under thumb pressure
Severe loss of grain market value and potential contamination with mycotoxins
culturalActions: Time sowing so grain maturation coincides with drier post-monsoon weather
Harvest crop promptly at physiological maturity without delaying in wet fields
Dry harvested heads quickly to below 10% moisture before threshing and storage
prevention: Grow mold-tolerant varieties with open or semi-loose panicles
Foliar spray of Propiconazole (1ml/L) or Mancozeb (2.5g/L) at 50% flowering if heavy rains persist
Clean and treat saved seed with thiram or captan (3g/kg seed)
Grain Mold.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Anthracnose.explanation: Sorghum Anthracnose (Colletotrichum sublineolum) causes circular to elliptical red/tan spots with distinct dark margins on foliage and stalk red rot.
symptoms: Small, circular to elliptic spots on leaf blades with tan/gray centers and prominent red-to-purple margins
Abundant tiny black fruiting bodies (acervuli) visible with a hand lens inside necrotic spots
Midrib red rot and stalk lodging during high wind storms
culturalActions: Chop and incorporate or burn infected sorghum crop residues after harvest
Rotate with non-grass broadleaf crops (soybean, cotton, sunflower)
Avoid high plant densities that trap humidity in the lower canopy
prevention: Seed treatment with certified fungicide (Carbendazim + Mancozeb at 2g/kg)
Plant anthracnose-tolerant hybrids
Ensure balanced potash application to strengthen stalk rind strength
Anthracnose.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: Pearl Millet (Bajra) exhibits vigorous drought-tolerant tillering, erect narrow leaves, sturdy culms, and long, densely packed cylindrical bristled earheads with uniform pearly grains.
symptoms: Clean erect narrow green leaf blades with no downy mildew or rust pustules
Uniform, tightly packed cylindrical earhead with healthy bristled spikelets
Sturdy culms with active tillers and clean root crown
culturalActions: Sow on ridges and furrows to optimize rainwater harvesting and prevent root waterlogging
Thin seedlings at 15-20 days to maintain 10-15 cm spacing between plants
Intercrop with moth bean, cowpea, or pigeon pea for drought resilience
prevention: Use certified hybrid seeds (Shraddha, Saburi, ICTP 8203, GHB 558)
Seed treatment with metalaxyl (Apron 35 SD at 6g/kg seed) to prevent downy mildew
Practice clean field cultivation and rogue out volunteer plants
Healthy.source: ICAR - AICRP on Pearl Millet (Jodhpur) & MPKV Rahuri
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Downy Mildew.explanation: Downy Mildew or 'Green Ear' disease (Sclerospora graminicola) is the most destructive disease of bajra in Maharashtra, transforming floral parts into leafy structures.
symptoms: Yellowing and chlorotic striping on young leaves, with white downy growth on undersides in early morning
Infected plants are stunted and produce excessive malformed tillers
Earhead transformed completely or partially into a mass of green leafy structures ('Green Ear')
culturalActions: Rogue and bury infected plants showing green ear symptoms before oospores mature in soil
Deep plow field immediately after harvest to bury oospores below the plow layer
Rotate with non-cereal crops for at least 2-3 years
prevention: Strict seed treatment with Metalaxyl-M (Apron XL at 2ml/kg seed)
Cultivate downy-mildew resistant hybrids certified by ICAR/State Universities
Foliar spray with Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (2g/L) at 20-25 days after sowing if leaf striping appears
Downy Mildew.source: ICAR - AICRP on Pearl Millet & MPKV Rahuri
Downy Mildew.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Rust.explanation: Bajra Rust (Puccinia substriata) produces reddish-orange to dark brown pustules on both leaf surfaces, drying up foliage during grain filling.
symptoms: Small, round to elliptical reddish-brown pustules on upper and lower leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture shedding powdery brown urediniospores
Leaves dry and wither prematurely, resulting in reduced grain weight and poor fodder quality
culturalActions: Eradicate alternate host brinjal (Solanum melongena) and weed species in vicinity
Harvest crop promptly once physiological maturity is attained
Avoid late Kharif or late summer sowings
prevention: Sow certified rust-tolerant bajra varieties
Foliar spray of wettable sulfur (3g/L) or Mancozeb (2g/L) upon early appearance of pustules
Maintain balanced crop nutrition
Rust.source: ICAR - AICRP on Pearl Millet & MPKV Rahuri
Rust.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: Turmeric (Halad - Salem/Pratibha) displays broad, lush green lanceolate leaves with long petioles, erect pseudostems, and vigorous underground rhizome clusters with bright orange/yellow flesh.
symptoms: Lush green, broad oblong foliage without leaf spots, blotches, or margins curling
Sturdy erect pseudostem free of water-soaked basal collar rotting
Healthy, plump mother and finger rhizomes with deep golden-yellow core
culturalActions: Plant on raised beds (1.2m wide, 15-20 cm high) with deep drainage furrows to prevent waterlogging
Apply abundant organic neem cake (2 tons/ha) and well-decomposed FYM at bed preparation
Mulch beds heavily with green leaves or sugarcane trash immediately after planting
prevention: Select disease-free healthy seed rhizomes from certified seed plots
Treat seed rhizomes before planting by dipping in Trichoderma viride (10g/L) suspension for 30 minutes
Crop rotation with maize, soybean, or sugarcane every 2-3 years
Healthy.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR) & VNMKV Parbhani
Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Rhizome Rot.explanation: Rhizome Rot or 'Kuj/Rot' (Pythium aphanidermatum / Fusarium solani) is the most destructive disease of turmeric in Sangli and Hingoli, causing basal soft rot and plant collapse.
symptoms: Yellowing of lower leaves progressing upwards along leaf margins
Basal collar region becomes soft, water-soaked, and decays with foul odor
Entire pseudostem pulls out easily from the rotting subterranean rhizome
culturalActions: Ensure perfect surface drainage; water stagnation even for 24 hours induces rapid rot
Carefully rogue out and destroy rotting clumps along with surrounding soil
Avoid injuring roots and rhizomes during weeding and earthing up
prevention: Dip seed rhizomes in Metalaxyl-Mancozeb (2g/L) + bio-formulation for 30 minutes before planting
Drench affected patches and surrounding beds with Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (2.5g/L) or Copper Oxychloride (3g/L)
Solarize soil and incorporate Trichoderma harzianum enriched FYM
Rhizome Rot.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Leaf Spot.explanation: Turmeric Leaf Spot (Colletotrichum capsici) causes elliptical to oblong brown spots with gray centers and yellow halos on upper leaves, leading to leaf scorching.
symptoms: Elliptical to oblong necrotic spots on both leaf surfaces, mostly on upper foliage
Spots have distinct grayish-white centers with dark brown raised margins and yellow halos
Coalescence of numerous spots leads to extensive leaf drying and premature defoliation
culturalActions: Collect and burn infected dried leaves after harvest to reduce resting fungal perithecia
Ensure proper shade regulation if turmeric is grown as an intercrop in fruit orchards
Provide adequate potassium nutrition to improve foliage resistance
prevention: Preventive foliar spray of Mancozeb (2.5g/L) or Carbendazim (1g/L) at first onset of spots
Dip seed rhizomes in bio-protective Trichoderma suspension before sowing
Follow 2-year crop rotation with non-host crops
Leaf Spot.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Healthy.explanation: Potato plants exhibit vigorous compound foliage, sturdy stems, healthy stolons, and active tuberization without foliar blight or ring rot.
symptoms: Vibrant green compound leaves with healthy leaflets
Erect sturdy stems with no blackleg or bacterial wilting
Healthy subterranean stolons and clean tubers with intact skin
culturalActions: Earth up soil properly around plant base to prevent tuber greening from sunlight
Maintain uniform soil moisture using drip or furrow irrigation without waterlogging
Harvest during dry weather and cure tubers in well-ventilated shade for 10-15 days
prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers certified by ICAR-CPRI
Treat seed tubers before planting with Trichoderma viride (5g/kg) or boric acid (3%)
Follow 3-year crop rotation avoiding tomato, brinjal, and chili

Healthy.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Early Blight.explanation: Early Blight (Alternaria solani) causes target-board dark brown spots with concentric rings on older potato leaves.

Chlorotic yellowing around lesions leading to premature leaf shedding
Dark sunken leathery lesions on potato tuber skin
culturalActions: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves promptly
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation that splashes fungal spores
Maintain wide row spacing to allow canopy air movement
prevention: Spray Mancozeb (2.5g/L) or Chlorothalonil (2g/L) preventively during warm humid periods
Apply balanced fertilizer avoiding excessive vegetative nitrogen
Deep plow crop residues after harvesting
Early Blight.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.

Late Blight.explanation: Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) is a catastrophic water mold causing rapid water-soaked brown lesions and white downy mildew on leaf undersides.
symptoms: Water-soaked irregular pale green patches turning rapidly dark brown to purplish-black
Fine white downy mildew growth on underside of leaves under humid cool conditions
Foul-smelling rotting of foliage and brown granular rot inside tubers
culturalActions: Destroy all volunteer potato plants and cull piles near fields
Hill up soil well over potato ridges to prevent zoospores washing down into tubers
Cut and destroy haulms 10-12 days prior to harvesting to prevent tuber infection
prevention: Spray systemic-contact fungicide (Metalaxyl + Mancozeb at 2.5g/L) upon disease forecast warning
Plant late blight resistant cultivars (Kufri Pukhraj, Kufri Jyoti, Kufri Khyati)
Store only clean, completely dry, cured tubers in cold storage
Late Blight.pesticideNote: Use only registered crop-protection products according to the label and local agricultural extension guidance.
